本迪爾框鼓是北非與西南亞的木框膜鳴鼓，屬框鼓家族，霍恩博斯特尔–薩克斯編號211: The bendir is a wooden-framed membranophone drum of North Africa and south-western Asia, belonging to the frame-drum family, Hornbostel–Sachs number 211.3. A gut snare string is often stretched across the head, which buzzes when the drum is struck with the fingers or the palm. It is played with the drum held upright, the thumb of the non-dominant hand passed through a hole in the frame. It is common in North African traditional music and Sufi ritual, and was also used in ancient Egypt and Mesopotamia.
本迪爾框鼓為北非與西亞的木框框鼓，屬傳統樂器，演奏範圍遍及北非，並用於蘇菲儀式；: The bendir is a wooden-framed frame drum of North Africa and western Asia, a traditional instrument played throughout North Africa and used in Sufi ritual; it was also used in ancient Egypt and Mesopotamia. It is classed as a membranophone drum, struck with the fingers or the palm. In Turkish, bendir means 'large palm frame drum'.

A gut snare string is usually fitted across the head, giving a buzzing timbre when struck. It is struck with the fingers or the palm, while the other hand's thumb passes through a hole in the frame to hold it. Apart from the wooden frame and the gut snare, the source does not state the materials of the other parts.
本迪爾框鼓的聆聽場合主要見於北非傳統音樂，也出現在蘇菲儀式中；亦見於古代埃及與美: The bendir is heard mainly in North African traditional music and also in Sufi ritual; it also appears on musical occasions in ancient Egypt and Mesopotamia. It is usually struck with the fingers or the palm, and if a gut string is fitted to the frame it gives a buzzing timbre. Beside the Egyptian tar drum, the bendir has a gut string at the back; beside the Irish bodhrán, it is not played with a stick.
本迪爾框鼓的音色主要由鼓面受手指或手掌敲擊產生；鼓背常張有腸線響弦，敲擊時會帶來: The timbre of the bendir comes mainly from the head struck by the fingers or the palm; a gut snare string is often stretched across the back, which gives a buzzing resonance when struck. It is played with the body vertical, the thumb of the non-dominant hand through a hole in the frame to hold it. Beside the Egyptian tar frame drum, the tar has no snare at the back of the frame; beside the Irish bodhrán, the bodhrán is struck with a stick. 演奏時將鼓保持垂直，非慣用手拇指穿過鼓框上的孔洞以支撐鼓身。發聲以手指或手掌直接: Hold the drum vertical, with the thumb of the non-dominant hand through a hole in the frame to support the body. The sound is made by striking the head directly with the fingers or the palm; a snare string, usually of gut, is often stretched across the head, and it buzzes when the drum is struck. A beginner can first practise holding the drum steady and vertical, then strike with the palm or the fingers, lightly and heavily, to feel the change of timbre that the snare brings.
